corrections.was: The second column is Opposition, the obstacles the player must overcome. Opposition is what makes a game fun, and it can also frustrate. Tennis has an opponent across the net, and a cereal race has the other racers. Eating cereal has nothing in the way. For example, an enemy that patrols back and forth on a narrow platform is opposition. The player wants the flag, and the enemy stands in the way.
corrections.now: The second column is Opposition, the obstacles the player must overcome. Opposition makes a game fun, and it can also frustrate. corrections.why: 'is what makes a game fun' made opposition the sole source of fun; the slide entry says only 'it makes a game fun and can frustrate', and slide 6 names six kinds of fun.

corrections.was: Now add one rule. The cube hurts the cells around it, then disappears. In this computed picture it hits eight cells. Nobody drew a fuse, yet the player sees a bomb. That is thematic feel at work, the rule alone says what the thing is. For example, a placeholder block that holds the player for a moment and then sinks away feels like a crumbling platform, before any art is made.
corrections.now: Now add one rule. The cube hurts the cells around it, then disappears. In this computed picture it hits the eight cells around its own square. Nobody drew a fuse, yet the player sees a bomb. That is thematic feel at work, the rule alone says what the thing is. For example, a placeholder block that holds the player for a moment and then sinks away feels like a crumbling platform, before any art is made.
corrections.why: Nine red cells are drawn (renderTheme fills the cube's own cell too) while the caption says 8 cells hit; the note counts (2r+1) squared minus the cube, so saying 'the eight cells around its own square' matches both the caption and the picture.

corrections.was: Widen the blast to two cells in every direction, and twenty-four cells are hit. Same cube, same lack of art, but the player now feels more danger and more power. One number in one rule changed the feeling. So art and mechanics must tell the same story. For example, if an enemy is drawn as a tiny harmless mouse but its attack covers half the screen, the look and the rule disagree, and the player feels cheated.
corrections.now: Widen the blast to two cells in every direction, and the twenty-four cells around its square are hit. Same cube, same lack of art, but the player now feels more danger and more power. One number in one rule changed the feeling. So art and mechanics must tell the same story. For example, if an enemy is drawn as a tiny harmless mouse but its attack covers half the screen, the look and the rule disagree, and the player feels cheated.
corrections.why: Twenty-five red cells are drawn while the caption says 24 cells hit; the note excludes the cube's own cell, so the narration now says the twenty-four cells around its square.
